dispersion_measure.description: Dispersion measure (DM) measures the integrated column density of free electrons along the line of sight, typically to a pulsar or fast radio burst, in units of cm^-3 pc.

redshift.description: Redshift (z) measures the relative stretching of light's wavelength due to cosmic expansion or relative motion, a dimensionless quantity.

flux.description: Flux density (S) measures the power received per unit area per unit frequency from an astronomical source, in janskys (Jy).

fluence.description: Fluence measures the time-integrated flux density of a transient event, in units of Jy ms, representing the total energy received per unit area.

luminosity.description: Luminosity (L) measures the total energy emitted per unit time by an astronomical source, in erg per second.

distance.description: Distance measures the line-of-sight separation between Earth and the astronomical source, in megaparsecs (Mpc).

event_rate.description: Event rate measures the volumetric occurrence rate of transient events, in units of events per cubic gigaparsec per year (Gpc^-3 yr^-1).

rotation_measure.description: Rotation measure (RM) quantifies the Faraday rotation of polarized radio emission caused by a magnetized plasma along the line of sight, in radians per square meter (rad m^-2).

scattering_timescale.description: Scattering timescale measures the temporal broadening of a pulse due to multipath propagation through an inhomogeneous plasma, in milliseconds.

spectral_index.description: Spectral index (α) quantifies the power-law slope of the flux density as a function of frequency, a dimensionless number typically defined such that flux ∝ ν^{α}.

magnetic_field.description: Magnetic field strength (B) measures the intensity of the magnetic field, in gauss (G), often along the line of sight or averaged over a region.

electron_density.description: Electron density (n_e) measures the number of free electrons per unit volume in a plasma, in particles per cubic centimeter (cm^-3).
